FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 October 1985, after the draft finalized by the Cosmetics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 IS : 435-1973* covers a number of sesame oil grades The present standard has been drawn variety of industries. fically to cater to the needs of the cosmetic industry. used in a up speci-

and solvent extracted are 0.3 Both the types of oil, namely expressed All other changes considered necessary covered in the present standard. to align the standard with others in the series for raw materials and finished cosmetics have been included. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-19607. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS : 11376- 1985 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description 3.1.1 Type 1 - The material shall be sesame oil obtained from clean Sesamum orientale and sound sesame seeds ( Sesamum indicum Linn, syn. Linn., fam. Pedaliaceae ) or good quality sesame cake by a process of expression or solvent extraction using solvent haxane conforming to The oil shall be refined by neutralization with alkali, IS : 3470-1966*. bleached with bleaching earth or activated carbon or both, and deodorised with steam. The oil shall be practically odourless or have a very mild odour characteristics of sesame oil.
material shall be sesame oil obtained from clean 3.1.2 TyFe 2 - The Sesamum orientale and sound sesame seeds ( Sesamum indicum Linn, syn. Pedaliaceae ) by a process of expression. The oil shall Linn., fam. have the characteristics odour of sesame oil. 3.2 The sediment, colouring material shall be clear and free from rancidity, adultrants, suspend and other foreign matter, separated water and added and flavouring substances.

3.3 Admixture with Other Oils - The material shall be free from admixture with other oils or adultrants, when tested according to the methods prescribed in IS : 548 ( Part 2 )-1976t. 3.4 The material Table 1. 4. PACKING shall also comply with the requirements given in

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ), Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that Details of conditions under which a licence for the standard as a further safeguard. use of the IS1 Certification Mark may he granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

ANNEX B [Table 1, S2No. (xii)]
DETERMINATION
B-1 REAGENTS B-1.l Glacial Acetic Acid

OF PEROXIDE VALUE

B-1.2 Chloroform B-1.3 Saturated Pdassium Iodide Solution -- 0.01 N

B-1.4 Sodium Thiosulphate

B-2 PROCEDURE Weigh 5.0 f 0.5 g of the sample "ina 250-ml glass-stoppered conical flask. Add 30 ml of a mixture of 3 volumes glacial acetic acid and 2 volumes of chloroform. Swirl until dissolved, and add 0.5 ml of saturated potassium io&de .soIution. Allow to stand for exactly 1 tnin, with occasional shaking, add 30 ml of water. Titrate gradually, with continuous and vigorous shaking, with 0.01 N sodium thiosulphate solution until the yellow colour almost disappears. Add 0.5 ml of starch solution, continue the titration, shaking vigorously until the blue colour just disappears (A). Carry out a blank determination under the same con&ion without adding any sample (8). The volume of 0.01 N sodium thiosulphate in the blank determination must not exceed 0.1 ml. 1
